comment: Dear Planning Commission, My husband and I have been residents in Lexington Village in Old Farm for over 10 years. We have been told that we can submit comments and concerns to the planning commission for consideration. I was out of town and unable to attend the Open House on May 5, however, I have spoken with several others who did attend and have obtained some of the information that was available, mainly the floor plans and the site plan. Here are the points I hope the committee will consider: 1. It seems premature to have this project before the planning commission when there are still a number of unknowns. In looking at the site plan, it appears it has not been updated with the latest floor plans, particularly the new ‘porches’ that have been added to the structures. I am particularly concerned about the three proposed units on the west side of the property. It looks like there is no setback from the current right of way that exists between the main parcel and the unbuildable parcel by the pond. And yet, it looks like there is a ‘patio’ added to the west side of structures D, E and F. Since there are no measurements on the floor plans, I can’t tell how far out that reaches but it is unclear how the developer proposes to accommodate that addition. 2. The site plan shows the above-mentioned right of way as a sidewalk instead of the current roadway that exists. I have been told they plan to keep it as a gravel roadway but that should be reflected on the site plan. 3. My biggest concern is about the proposed height of the structures. Apparently, at the open house the developer would not commit to what that height will be, only saying they can be ‘up to 32 feet’. Earlier in this process, when the HOA took the first vote for allowing the project to join the HOA, they stated that the one and half story units would be 26 feet high. I’m not sure why there are no heights on the floor plan documents, but it would seem that should be decided at this point and another reason why this is premature. 4. I object to these units being called ‘ramblers’ because they are, in fact, two-story units. The livable space on the upper floor consists of a bedroom, full bathroom, two closets, one large storage area, and a ‘loft’ open space. The square footage appears to be similar to the square footage in the basement. Especially if the height of the buildings will be anywhere close to 32 feet, it is a two-story unit. Although it is 1 difficult to tell because there appears to be no square footage measurements on the plans or I cannot tell how to read that. 5. All of the other buildings in Lexington Village are true ‘ramblers’ with finished square footage above the first floor. The current maximum heights of the existing units is 18 feet at the peak of some of the garages, but more like 15 feet at the peak of the existing main buildings. The proposed units will TOWER over the existing units at around twice the height and will not blend in with the existing units. 6. It’s my understanding that true one-story units do ‘not pencil out’ for the developer and why they are forced to go up and develop more finished square footage. 7. In my opinion, the size of the land parcel does not support the development of these large units. If you take away the unbuildable portion of the parcel by the pond, the density of the units and especially with the height will feel very crowded and again, not consistent with the existing units. 8. I have also heard comments that the developer is planning to move the entire project some number of feet to the south, however, this is not reflected anywhere on the site plan. It is important for the residents to understand what exactly is being proposed. Again, why this action is premature. 9. I am concerned about the number of mature trees that will be removed to accommodate this project. The trees and landscaping are what lends the ambience and character of Lexington Village. I have a dog that I walk 3-4 times a day around the property and enjoy the landscaping, trees, grass, and open space and fear this new development will destroy the existing feeling and views, especially along the pond. The Lexington Village HOA will hold another vote once all of the final dimensions, square footage, height, and all of the agreements between the developer and the HOA are finalized. If the developer keeps changing previous commitments it may be that more of the owners will change their mind about allowing them into the HOA. Please consider these items as the development goes through the planning process with Millcreek City.

Dear Mr. Murray, Here are my comments regarding the project as presented at the open house by the developer, Matt Knight, and some background information. I live in Lexington Village and have owned a condo there for over 22 years. My husband and I bought a condo there because of the open common areas, pond, the ambience, and its rich history. My husband was an architectural historian. All of the condos in Lexington Village are one-story, except for one brick two-story house that is original to the property. That house is well-hidden by trees and faces Old Farm Road, not Old Farm Way. The planned development does not consist of one-story condos. The developer at the meeting, and at prior times when he has discussed the project with Lexington Village HOA members, refers to the condos as ramblers. They are not ramblers. They are huge one and a half story structures that according to the developer will be 32-feet tall or possibly some might be a couple of feet shorter. He was very vague about the height, but he did have elevations that did not include measurements. When asked about the square footage, he said six of the condos would be around 3,000 square feet and the three closest to the pond would be around 3,500 square feet and then he changed it to maybe around 4,000 square feet. Again, he gave vague answers. Since it was an open house regarding the project, I would’ve expected him to be better prepared. On prior occasions when the developer met with Lexington Village HOA members, he said the condos would be 26 feet tall. Even at that height, they would be appreciably taller than the 3 Sean Murray, planner Page 2 May 6, 2026 current condos, which are 15 feet at the roof peak located at the side of the buildings. So, the front of the condos is much shorter. The manor house units do have garages that are 18 feet at the peak, but they can’t be seen from the road or sidewalks. You can only see the garages if you drive down one of the driveways. The planned condos don’t fit in with Lexington Village condos. All of the current 77 condos have private courtyards. They don’t exist in the proposed project. The private outdoor space per unit in the project is minimal because the condos, roads and sidewalks fill most of the buildable area in the .94 acre property. The 32-foot condos would tower over all 77 existing condos, disrupting the neighborhood’s scale and overwhelming the low profile of the current community. They will also have a significant impact on the ambience, character, and Lexington Village’s deep-rooted history. The Lexington Village HOA did have a preliminary vote whether or not to allow the project in our HOA. It did receive the required 2/3rd yes votes, but the members were not voting on the design. The Lexington Village owners that I talked to, which was a significant number, who voted “yes” did it because of the following concerns: the units could turn into rental properties, possibly become Air B and B’s, and we could not police the new buyers from parking on our private street, in guest parking areas, or enjoying our common areas and they wouldn’t be paying dues for the maintenance. Having them in the HOA would give the HOA control over those concerns and the buyers would be paying dues. In closing, please take into consideration that every condo in Lexington Village is a single story. The introduction of 32-foot structures would stand out dramatically, dominating the skyline and overshadowing the surrounding condos. And Lexington Village is unique, no other condominiums in Millcreek have a park-like setting, a pond, and a storied history.

Hi there Sean First off. Thanks for what you do and especially Thanks for answering my questions and listening to me vent over the past year or so. You have been very good about returning calls and helpful getting answers. We are newcomers to Lexington Village. (2nd year).. Our property butts on to the North West side of the project property. We moved here because of the open space, the Trees/Greenery/Pond etc that create the ambiance of Old Farm. Our Concerns with this Development are: 1. Height 32 ft is overwhelming compared to our units which are half the size. 2. Size 3,000 to 4,500 square feet. Matt from J Development mentioned the new units were geared for “Empty Nesters” why so big.? 3. No Green Space. Squeezing 9 units onto less than an acre is a little extreme. It seems to be more about making a buck than fitting into the Old Farm Community. These buildings will be so encroaching and out of place. Please take our concerns into consideration when deciding on the plans put forth by J Development.
